reason: The commit reorganizes existing request-body handling without adding a new entry point, protocol feature, configuration requirement, initialization requirement, or input constraint. The HTTP/1 and HTTP/2 harness paths still call h2o_http1_accept and h2o_http2_accept with arbitrary request bytes, so they continue to exercise the modified parsing and body-processing logic. Streaming selection is moved from the shared h2o_write_req_first callback into protocol-specific write_req_first functions, while body buffers and byte counts are relocated to connection/stream structures. These internal changes do not require a different harness API or state setup.
evidence: fuzz/driver.cc directly invokes h2o_http1_accept or h2o_http2_accept after passing the complete fuzzer-controlled Data and Size through feeder.

The diff replaces req->_req_body.bytes_received with req->req_body_bytes_received and moves req->_req_body.body to conn->req_body, stream->req_body, or the HTTP/3 stream; corresponding initialization and disposal are updated.
h2o_write_req_first and on_request_streaming_selected are replaced by protocol-local write_req_first implementations that preserve the existing decision based on supports_request_streaming.
The existing registered handlers, host configuration, timeouts, accept context, and HTTP/1 or HTTP/2 initialization APIs remain valid and unchanged.

The HTTP/3 edits only relocate its request-body buffer and lifecycle handling; they do not introduce HTTP/3 support or a new externally testable feature that would make the existing HTTP/1 and HTTP/2 harnesses inadequate.
recommended_action: Keep the existing fuzz harness unchanged; routine regression execution is sufficient.
